gates.finding: Historical #538 establishes a common paper-level PolyBench task order, batch loop, solver/evolver policy, zero temperatures and result surface for the named auto-harness rows.
Adaptive Auto-Harness explicitly identifies its SkillOS baseline as Ouyang et al. (2026), SkillOS: Learning Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents, arXiv:2605.06614.

The public AdaptiveHarness release explicitly states that the SkillOS comparison implementation is not shipped. The inspected A-Evolve pre-release revision e4f70b949989e0abf08532e8223cb9eab447e971 contains recoverable GEPA and Meta-Harness implementation paths but no SkillOS implementation path in its recursive tree, and inspected commit-history search does not expose a SkillOS implementation binding.
gates.blocking_effect: Do not attribute the reported PolyBench SkillOS row to any public SkillOS repository or reproduction until first-party primary evidence binds the evaluated implementation and immutable revision.

gates.finding: Because the producing SkillOS implementation is not publicly identified, no immutable evaluated repository revision can be credited from the current evidence.

A standalone assessment of a future first-party SkillOS repository would be a separate system-in-focus decision. Third-party reproductions must not be substituted for the implementation evaluated by Adaptive Auto-Harness.
Paper-level matching and method identity do not establish native/adapter-preserved implementation attribution, so the SkillOS row cannot enter a matched canonical S4 cell.
